_comment: Machine-extracted saint biographical anchors. UNREVIEWED. Dates are kept verbatim as the source expresses them, never normalised. Not merged until a human signs off.
_method: Every one of the 169 rows of the shrine corpus was read (human-figure rows in full; deity/temple rows filtered for any date, title or name statement), then the 39 files in shrine_entries/ and the 10 in entries/ plus entries/web-research-2026-08/. Nothing here comes from model knowledge: every value is a substring of, or a literal reading of, the quoted source text. An automated check asserts that every `quote` in this file is a verbatim substring of its named source (whitespace normalised); it exits non-zero otherwise. The checker asserts, per proposal: (1) every `quote` and every variant quote is a verbatim substring of its named source with whitespace normalised; (2) every 3- or 4-digit year appearing in born/died/floruit occurs literally in that source text — this is the rule that catches a year supplied from model priors, and it fired twice during authoring and was fixed both times; (3) precision is one of the seven allowed values, calendar one of four, confidence one of {0.95, 0.7}; (4) saintIsNew agrees with membership in the KG saint list; (5) shrineSlug resolves to a corpus row or a repo file; (6) precision "unrecorded" cannot carry a born value. The script was written at scratchpad path build/check.py during this task and is NOT yet in the repository — it belongs in pipeline/ (see CLAUDE.md RULE 0 and RULE 4) if these proposals are taken forward.

_fields.born/died: verbatim as the source expresses it, including hedges ("around 1720", "the first half of the 1100s", "25 Rabiʿ al-Thani; year not stated"). Empty string means the source gives nothing, which is itself the finding.
_fields.floruit: used where a source gives only a century or a reign window and no birth or death year; never promoted into born/died.
_fields.precision: exact-date | year | circa | range | century | disputed | unrecorded. "unrecorded" is used only where the source positively states the dates are unknown.
_fields.confidence: 0.95 explicit and unambiguous; 0.7 hedged ("is said to", "traditionally", "generally held"), identity uncertain, or the source is self-published/interested.
